The ICTs are widely used in such protests. Same situation is with low earth orbit satellite internet communication systems. Let me bring some examples. Fall 2022, Iran, anti-governmental protests. And very important thing is that Starlink system terminals illegally imported to Iran were used during these protests. After that, Iran went to the Radio Regulation Board, RRB, of the International Telecommunication Union, ITU. And after long time deliberations, 94th meeting of the RRB proclaimed that this case was indirect contraversion of the provisions of the ITU regulations and resolutions. In this respect, telecommunication administrations of the states associated with Starlink were requested to take immediate actions to disable Starlink terminals operating within the territory of Iran. It is very important because it was the first official confirmation of the use of low earth orbit satellite internet communication system in violation of the principle of non-interference into the state's affairs. Completely same situation happened in Venezuela during protests before the presidential elections in this country. Again, Starlink terminals, again illegally imported terminals, and again they were used to coordinate protests. completely same as in Iran. As all of us know quite well from the media, that even the United States administration some time ago officially questioned the reliability of the Starlink system. And of course, we are talking not only about Starlink, it is an example, don't get me wrong, there are a lot of such systems operating. OneWeb, Amazon Kupier, and many, many others. So what are the risks of such systems? Let's sum up. First one, the use of satellite communication terminals to provide broadband internet access to users, bypassing national information space control systems poses huge risk of interference in the internal affairs of states. This type of system can be used to organize and coordinate protests, establish uncontrolled information transmission channels and conduct mass broadcasts in violation of national legislation of states. Second one, the use of spacecraft for military purposes, including for reconnaissance in the optical and radio frequency spectrum during satellite flights over the national territory of member states. for controlling unmanned systems and for providing communication channels in combat zones is also the risk. Thus, some commercial communication systems are being used to control attack drones and remotely operated boats during the Russia's special military operation in Ukraine. The onboard equipment of these systems includes satellite terminals of various systems, preliminary Starlink. This allows to use unmanned systems at significant distances from their operators, including during attacks on port infrastructure in the Russian cities of Sevastopol, Novorossiysk, the Crimean bridge, and many, many other targets. Furthermore, such terminals are being used by rocket system crews to coordinate strikes on civilian infrastructure in Russia's border regions, such as the Kursk region. What should we do in this situation? How can we protect states from the threats outlined above? We are currently working closely within the International Telecommunications Union and within the COPUOS Committee on Peaceful Uses of Outer Space of the United Nations. In the ITU, the use of radio spectrum and orbits for satellite communication systems is regulated by the Radio Regulations, an international treaty updated every four years at the World Radiocommunication Conferences. Currently, the Radio Regulations do not limit, unfortunately, do not limit the inclusion of states in the non-geostationary orbit service area, yet the number of such systems and the satellites they are used is growing. At the World Radio Communication Conference in 2023, Resolution 14 was adopted instructing states to conduct studies on the development and implementation of regulatory measures to limit unauthorized operation of earth stations on non-geostationary orbits. Furthermore, this item is included on the agenda for the World Radio Communication Conference to be held in 2027.
